study: Rain to river: how long after rain upstream each gauge rises and crests
question: For each gauge with a reviewed watershed outline: after a rain over the watershed, how many hours until the gauge starts to rise and until it crests, and is that steady enough from storm to storm to tell people?
what_was_known_when_this_was_written: The list of research basins, their review status and drainage areas, and which gauges have a discharge record (row counts and first dates only).

That NOAA's archive lists the hourly and 24-hour gauge-corrected files for sample days from 2020 to 2026, and that USGS serves 15-minute discharge for past dates. One hourly file was downloaded to learn its size.
No watershed rain total and no discharge value in the study window was read, plotted, compared or summarised before this file was committed.
outcome_for_every_gauge: Each gauge in scope ends with one of two results: a lag range that passed every rule under release_rule, or one named reason from reasons_for_no_range. There is no third state and no manual override.

scope.in: Every row of rainfall_research_basins with review_status 'reviewed' and enabled true on 2026-11-18.

not_studied.why: The rain total is only as good as the outline it is averaged over.

dam_controlled.why: Flow at these gauges is set by releases from a storage dam upstream, so a rise is the dam's schedule and not the rain's travel time. docs/rainfall-history.md excludes dam-controlled reaches from lag measurement.

sites.07057370: White River near Norfork: below Bull Shoals Dam
sites.07060500: White River at Calico Rock: below Bull Shoals and Norfork dams
sites.07063000: Black River at Poplar Bluff: below Clearwater Dam

included_with_a_note.06923950: Niangua River at Tunnel Dam: at a small hydroelectric diversion with no flood storage. It is studied by the same rules as every other gauge.

rain.product: NOAA MRMS MultiSensor_QPE_01H_Pass2 (gauge-corrected), one file an hour, from https://noaa-mrms-pds.s3.amazonaws.com
rain.watershed_amount: The area-weighted mean over the reviewed outline, by the same code the public rain view uses (mrmsTile, basinWeights, weightedRain) on the collector's tile. An hour with under 95% of the watershed covered has no amount.
rain.hour: The file stamped T covers the hour ending at T. It is stored as the hour starting at T minus one hour.
rain.screen: To avoid downloading hours with no rain, each day (the 24 hours ending 12:00 UTC) is first read from the 24-hour product (MultiSensor_QPE_24H_Pass2). If no gauge in scope has 0.05 in or more for the day, the day's 24 hourly files are not fetched and every hour is recorded as 0. If the 24-hour file is missing, the hourly files are fetched anyway.
rain.missing: An hourly file NOAA does not have, or one that fails to decode after three tries, leaves that hour with no amount for every gauge.

flow.service: USGS instantaneous values, parameter 00060 (discharge, cfs), https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/iv/
flow.hourly: Mean of the readings inside each clock hour. An hour with no numeric reading has no flow. Provisional data are used as served.
flow.no_record: A gauge USGS serves no discharge for in the window gets reason no_flow_record. Stage is not substituted.

sources.watershed_area: Geodesic area of the reviewed outline, in square miles.

storm.wet_hour: Watershed rain of 0.01 in or more in the hour.
storm.spell: Consecutive wet hours, joined across dry gaps shorter than 12 hours. A spell ends when 12 hours in a row are not wet.
storm.qualifies: Spell total of 0.50 in or more, and no more than 36 hours from its first wet hour to its last.
storm.rain_start: The moment 10% of the spell's rain had fallen, placed inside its hour in proportion.
storm.rain_centre: The moment 50% of the spell's rain had fallen, placed the same way.

set_aside.long_rain: Spell total of 0.50 in or more but longer than 36 hours.
set_aside.rain_record_incomplete: An hour with no rain amount inside the spell, in the 48 hours before it, or between it and the crest.
set_aside.wet_before: 0.25 in or more over the watershed in the 48 hours before the spell's first wet hour.
set_aside.outside_window: The 48 hours before the spell or its response window runs past either end of the study window.

response.baseline: Median hourly flow in the 6 hours before the spell's first wet hour. At least 4 of the 6 must have flow.
response.search: From the spell's first wet hour to the end of the window.
response.crest: The highest hourly flow in the search, at the first hour it is reached. Its time is the middle of that hour.
response.responded: Crest minus baseline is at least 25% of baseline and at least 5 cfs.
response.rise_begins: The first hour in the search, at or before the crest, whose flow is at least baseline plus 10% of (crest minus baseline). Its time is the middle of that hour.

set_aside.flow_record_incomplete: Baseline cannot be formed, or more than 10% of the hours in the search have no flow.
set_aside.no_crest_in_window: The river responded but the crest falls in the last 6 hours of the window, so it may still have been rising.
set_aside.rain_again_before_crest: The river responded but 0.25 in or more fell between the spell's last wet hour and the crest.
set_aside.rising_before_rain: The river responded but rise_begins is earlier than rain_start, or the crest is not after rain_centre.

response.counted: A storm is counted when it qualifies and nothing above sets it aside. A counted storm either responded or did not.

all_must_hold.enough_storms: At least 8 counted storms that responded.
all_must_hold.both_years: At least 3 of them in each study year.
all_must_hold.more_than_one_season: They come from at least 2 seasons, and no single season holds more than 75% of them.
all_must_hold.usually_responds: There are at least 4 counted storms of 1.00 in or more, and at least half of them responded.
all_must_hold.steady: For time_to_crest across the responding storms: the 90th percentile is no more than 3 times the 10th, or the two are no more than 6 hours apart.
all_must_hold.years_agree: The median time_to_crest of the two study years are within 3 hours of each other, or the larger is no more than 1.5 times the smaller.

release_rule.percentiles: Linear interpolation between ordered values (the common 'type 7' definition).

published.time_to_crest: 10th to 90th percentile, rounded outward to whole hours.
published.time_to_rise: 10th to 90th percentile, rounded outward to whole hours, and only when time_to_rise passes the 'steady' test on its own. Otherwise only the crest range is published.
published.always_with: The number of storms behind the range.

reasons_for_no_range.watershed_not_reviewed: Outside the study: the watershed outline has not been reviewed.
reasons_for_no_range.dam_controlled: Flow is set by a storage dam upstream.
reasons_for_no_range.no_flow_record: USGS serves no discharge for the gauge in the window.
reasons_for_no_range.uneven_years: Fewer than 3 responding storms in one study year.
reasons_for_no_range.one_season: Responding storms come from one season, or one season holds more than 75%.
reasons_for_no_range.seldom_responds: Fewer than 4 counted storms of 1.00 in or more, or fewer than half of them responded.
reasons_for_no_range.too_variable: Time to crest fails the 'steady' test.
reasons_for_no_range.years_disagree: The two study years fail the 'years_agree' test.

reason_order: A gauge that fails more than one rule is given the first failing reason in the order listed under reasons_for_no_range. Every failing rule is still recorded in the results.
what_a_released_range_may_be_used_for: A sentence in the weather section, for that gauge only, worded as a usual range and never as a prediction for one storm. The wording needs the owner's approval. A range is not evidence that rain has arrived or passed (docs/noaa-rainfall-plan.md).
what_this_study_replaces: The eight per-river lag estimates in river_characteristics.rain_lag_hours and the deprecated RAIN_LAG map, which have no recorded source.
changes_after_locking: Any change to a rule after the first results are seen is listed in README.md under 'Changes after locking', with the reason and the effect on every gauge's result. A fix to code that did not do what this file says is listed there too.
